name: known-gaps
note: Documented known gaps: strings where the engine and Chrome resolve glyphs differently and the layer-1 delta exceeds tolerance. Each entry records the divergence mechanism; the ledger carries the observed per-string numbers. The verify script asserts each of these still diverges (so a closed gap surfaces for reclassification), and the corpus stays green only because each has a documented reason.

measureText.reason: Five font-fallback divergences where skia resolves glyphs differently than Chrome's fontconfig fallback: proportional-font tabs, mixed-script runs, and Arabic punctuation/letter-spacing. The Thai and emoji-smiley entries were reclassified into the pass corpus (thai/, emoji/) once a Thai-capable face (Noto Sans Thai) and an emoji-capable face were registered and the strings were measured on the faces where glyph resolution agrees. Each remaining entry carries its divergence mechanism; docs/ledgers/text-measure.md records the observed per-string deltas, and the fixture note is the owner of record.
measureText.sunset: Reclassify each entry into the pass corpus when skia's font fallback matches Chrome's per-glyph fallback and tab-stop semantics (e.g. an emoji-capable face registered system-wide or engine-side fontconfig-style fallback). No entry may be removed without its divergence first closing.

entries.reason: Proportional-font tabs: Chrome's canvas applies tab-stop semantics (a tab advances to the next tab stop) while skia returns the font's raw U+0009 advance. Monospace tabs agree (see tabs/); this is the proportional-font tab case.

Mixed-script string: Chrome resolves each missing glyph through its per-glyph fallback (CJK and emoji faces), while skia keeps the whole run in Noto Sans. Single-script strings in one font agree (see cjk/, rtl/); mixed runs diverge.

entries.reason: Mixed-script fallback: Chrome shapes Latin and Japanese through fallback faces rather than the registered CJK face; skia keeps the run in Droid Sans Fallback.
Latin punctuation (!) in an Arabic run: Chrome falls the ASCII glyph back to a Latin face while skia keeps it in Droid Arabic Kufi. Pure-script Arabic and Arabic-Indic digits agree (see rtl/).

Letter-spacing on a joining script: Chrome does not apply ctx.letterSpacing to Arabic, while the engine's letter-spacing model adds spacing after every codepoint. Latin and CJK letter-spacing agree (see letter-spacing/).
